subject: Renewal: Dedicated capacity increase & burst model options
thread_summary: Renewal negotiation for BrightAI focused on adding reserved GPU capacity at renewal, defining burst/overflow behavior (on-demand vs hard cap), throughput guarantees, hot-start SLA, and pricing for hybrid model.
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@brightai.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightAI Procurement <procurement@brightai.io>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: BrightAI renewal: capacity planning and burst strategy

Neha —

As we approach our renewal (dec 1), we need to lock down the capacity plan. Over the last 9 months our peak utilization is up ~3x and we expect another 30–40% growth H1. We currently run a 40-GPU reserved pool with your Dedicated product. For the renewal we are evaluating:

- Option A: increase reserved GPUs permanently by +20 (predictable but higher committed cost)
- Option B: keep baseline reserved and rely on on-demand spillover (burst) during peak windows — we need clear billing and hard limits

Key asks from procurement: predictable month-to-month cost, a maximum hard cap for billing exposure, and an SLA around how long it takes to get additional burst capacity warmed up (we care about cold-start latency for realtime apps).

Can you share concrete options (pricing delta, throughput guarantees p95/p99, hot-start expectations) and a recommended default for our renewal term (12 vs 24 months)?

Thanks —
Olivia
Customer Success Lead, BrightAI

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@brightai.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T15:04:00Z
Subject: Re: BrightAI renewal: capacity planning and burst strategy

Olivia —

Thanks for the clear ask. I ran this by product and infra and sketched three practical paths for renewal. Attached is a short proposal PDF with line-item pricing. Summary below:

1) Conservative reserved increase (Baseline committed)
   - Add +20 GPUs to your reserved pool (baseline 60 GPUs)
   - Throughput guarantee: baseline sustained throughput at p95 for your primary text-gen route (configurable per-route), SLA credit if p95 exceeds agreed latency more than 4x/month
   - Pricing: +35% residual over your current reserved spend (monthly commit)

2) Hybrid (recommended for volatility)
   - Keep a smaller reserved bump (+10 GPUs) and enable burst up to +50 GPUs on-demand ON TOP of reserved cap
   - Burst billing: per-GPU-hour at a predefined burst rate (flat multiplier) capped monthly by a configurable hard cap you set (so procurement exposure is bounded)
   - Hot-start: we can offer "pre-warm" windows for predictable peaks (see proposal) and a guaranteed median warm-up <60s for pre-warmed pools; non-pre-warmed on-demand hot-starts are typically 60–120s depending on image and model
   - Pricing: lower committed uplift (+18%) + burst budget line item; includes 2 weeks free grace during cutover

3) On-demand only (low commit)
   - No reserved increase; rely fully on on-demand capacity with dynamic autoscale
   - Cheaper committed cost, but higher per-usage bill and less predictability; we can set a hard cap to limit monthly spend but that can lead to throttling at the cap

Open items for us to confirm: your preferred maximum monthly burst exposure (we typically see customers use caps between 20–50 GPU-hours/day), whether you want pre-warmed windows for daily traffic spikes, and term length (12 vs 24 mo).

I attached the proposal PDF. I propose a quick call with your procurement & infra to align and finalize the order form.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: RI_Dedicated_Proposal_Q4.pdf (proposal summary, pricing tables, sample SLA language)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@brightai.io>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T11:28:00Z
Subject: Re: BrightAI renewal: capacity planning and burst strategy

Hi Olivia —

Quick technical clarifications from infra/SE side to help procurement decide between hybrid vs hard-cap-only:

- Throughput guarantees are measured at p95 for the configured API route and include any queued latency from batching; we can publish per-route profiles in the order form.
- If you choose a hard cap on burst, we will queue and then throttle requests once the cap is hit (your app-level retries will see 429s unless you want a graceful fallback to a lower-cost model).
- Pre-warm behavior: pre-warmed GPUs keep model weights hot and KV caches warm — this yields sub-60s hot-start for most LLMs; without pre-warm, container startup + kernel JIT can take 60–140s depending on model size and quantization.
- We can offer a runbook for predictable daily bursts (scheduled pre-warm) to reduce cost while meeting latency SLOs.

If procurement wants hard exposure limits, hybrid + hard cap is the usual win: baseline reserved for steady state + burst-at-flat-rate with a monthly cap for spend control.

-Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@brightai.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightAI Procurement <procurement@brightai.io>
Date: 2026-11-05T08:09:00Z
Subject: Re: BrightAI renewal: capacity planning and burst strategy

Thanks Neha/Marissa — getting closer. Procurement has two non-negotiables for us to recommend to execs:

1) Billing exposure must be bounded by a contractual monthly hard cap (we can pick the number, but it must be explicit in the order form). If you offer hybrid with burst, the cap must apply to burst spend only (reserved is committed obviously).
2) We need a hot-start SLA addressed in contract language: we cannot accept multi-minute cold-starts for critical endpoints. Ideally we want a guaranteed warm-up of additional GPUs to be ready for traffic within 60s when requested. If you can't commit to 60s, propose the best concrete alternative and include credit structure tied to missed hot-starts.

Also the term: procurement prefers 12 months this cycle to keep flexibility, but will consider 24 if the economics materially improve.

Can you send a redline-friendly SLA amendment and a sample order form with a burst cap field populated with two pricing scenarios (cap at $10k/mo vs $25k/mo) so we can model both?

Olivia

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@brightai.io>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-09T16:37:00Z
Subject: Re: BrightAI renewal: capacity planning and burst strategy

Olivia —

Appreciate the procurement constraints. We can accommodate a bounded hybrid approach with concrete SLA language. Proposed commercial & SLA changes (high level):

- Baseline: +10 reserved GPUs (from 40 -> 50) for a 12-month term at a +18% committed uplift.
- Burst: allow burst up to +50 GPUs on top of reserved. Burst billed at a flat per-GPU-hour rate. We will include two capped options in the order form: $10k/mo cap and $25k/mo cap (burst only).
- Hot-start SLA: we will offer a contractual warm-up SLA for pre-warmed windows: median warm-up <60s; for on-demand cold starts we propose a 75s median SLA (we can push to 70s with an expansion credit).
- Credits: if warm-up SLA misses by >50% of attempts in a month, apply a pro-rated credit against that month's burst invoice (we'll include explicit credit tables in the redline).
- Pre-warm program: free pre-warm for two 2-hour windows/day during predictable peaks (no charge for the pre-warm time but counts against burst cap if used outside windows).

I'll attach a draft SLA amendment for redline and include a sample order form pre-populated for both cap scenarios. If this looks good to you I can route to legal and get the order form/Docusign ready for signature.

Thanks —
Dev Patel
VP, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA-amendment-draft.docx
Link: https://www.docusign.com/1234-orderform

From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@brightai.io>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightAI Procurement <procurement@brightai.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T14:53:00Z
Subject: Re: BrightAI renewal: capacity planning and burst strategy

Dev —

Thanks for the thoughtful proposal. BrightAI is comfortable moving to the hybrid model with the following modifications before we sign:

- Hot-start SLA: can you tighten the on-demand cold-start median SLA to 75s (you proposed 75s but earlier notes ranged up to 90s) and include a credit of 5% of that month's burst spend if the 75s median is missed more than twice in a month?
- Burst cap scenario: we will pilot with the $10k/mo capped burst for Q1, with an option to move to $25k/mo if growth dictates. Please reflect the $10k cap in the order form and call it out as a pilot for months 1–3.
- Expansion incentive: BrightAI requests a one-time 10% credit on committed uplift for the first full billing month after activation to offset migration/engineering costs.

Next step: please send the updated order form + redlineable SLA with the tightened 75s clause and the 10% one-time uplift credit, and we'll circulate internally. If legal signs off, we'll e-sign and target activation on Dec 1.

I'll await the updated pack — thanks again.

Olivia
Customer Success Lead, BrightAI
